aiExplanation: This function finds the **minimum number of moves** needed to make every element in `nums` equal, where a move changes one element by `1`. The key insight is that the best target value is the **median** of the array, because the median minimizes the total absolute distance to all other points. The code first sorts `nums` in ascending order, then picks the median: if the length is odd (checked with the bitwise `nums.length & 1`), it takes the exact middle element `nums[(nums.length - 1) / 2]`; if the length is even, it averages the two middle elements and rounds down with `Math.floor`. Finally, it loops over every number, adds `Math.abs(num - mid)` (how far each value is from the median) to `res`, and returns that total as the answer.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function computes the **fewest moves** required to make all values in `nums` identical, where each move increments or decrements a single element by `1`. It relies on the fact that moving everything toward the **median** always gives the smallest total cost. After sorting the array in ascending order, it computes `halfLen` as the floored half of the length so the middle index only needs to be calculated once. If the array length is odd (tested with `nums.length & 1`), the median is simply `nums[halfLen]`; if it is even, the median is the floored average of the two central elements `nums[halfLen - 1]` and `nums[halfLen]`. The loop then sums `Math.abs(num - median)` for every element, which is the number of single-step moves each value needs to reach the median, and that running total `res` is returned.
